main_finding: Euclidean methods outperform Mahalanobis on BLIND TEST

1_artifact_of_unknown_composition.description: Euclidean better because UNKNOWN species are taxon-distant
1_artifact_of_unknown_composition.test: Stratify UNKNOWN by taxonomic distance (SAME_FAMILY vs DIFFERENT_FAMILY)
1_artifact_of_unknown_composition.result: INCOMPLETE - both UNKNOWN species outside known genera
1_artifact_of_unknown_composition.conclusion: Cannot falsify via data (insufficient diversity in UNKNOWN)

2_artifact_of_known_composition.description: Results biased by specific KNOWN species distribution
2_artifact_of_known_composition.result: NOT_PERFORMED - would require re-splitting KNOWN clean
2_artifact_of_known_composition.note: Single VALIDATION/BLIND split may not generalize

3_artifact_of_class_imbalance.test: Check if FAR consistent across methods (it is: 0.18 for Euclidean)
3_artifact_of_class_imbalance.result: FAR similar between Euclidean and Cosine (both 0.18)
3_artifact_of_class_imbalance.interpretation: FAR not causing differential method performance

4_mahalanobis_threshold_misaligned.description: Official threshold (39.354) is from different CALIBRATION set
4_mahalanobis_threshold_misaligned.result: DONE - optimal_tau=88.75, Youden=1.0 on VALIDATION (unrealistic perfect)
4_mahalanobis_threshold_misaligned.interpretation: VALIDATION too small (all KNOWN), no UNKNOWN for threshold selection

critical_limitation.implication: Cannot select threshold based on KNOWN/UNKNOWN balance
critical_limitation.effect: Optimal thresholds (Youden=1.0) are artifacts of perfect separation in all-KNOWN subset
critical_limitation.solution_required: Separate CALIBRATION pool with mixed KNOWN/UNKNOWN
